shots.text: When I came back, the workers had already carried me to the waste chamber.
shots.note: The waste chamber: a heap of dead ants.

shots.text: Ants don't bury their dead, they just throw them out.
shots.note: A worker tips a body onto the pile.

shots.text: Nobody stays to say goodbye. Nobody even checks twice.
I woke up under the weight of a hundred bodies, old workers, broken soldiers, ants I used to walk beside.
shots.note: Buried under bodies; his eye opens.

shots.text: I pushed my way out, one leg at a time, and the green in my veins glowed brighter with every step.
So I climbed out of a pile of bodies, walked back into the colony, and nobody noticed.
The same ants who threw me away two days ago walked right past me.
One even bumped into me and said sorry, like I was a stranger.
shots.note: A sister bumps into him, pauses, walks on.

shots.text: And that's when I realized being invisible might be my greatest weapon.
shots.note: The green glint in his eye.
